transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. I came in because I’ve barely been sleeping since this warehouse inspection I had to do for work. I just lie there in bed replaying bits of it in my head. And when I do actually manage to drift off, I wake up sweaty and completely wide awake, like I’m right back near that blast. I just need some help getting some sleep.
How long ago did this warehouse blast happen?
It's been about a week. The explosion happened while I was doing the inspection, and, yeah, this has all been going on ever since then.
Since the explosion, have you found yourself going out of your way to avoid reminders, places, or thoughts related to what happened?

Yeah, I have. At work, I've been completely avoiding the file for that warehouse. I've also been letting any calls about our industrial accounts just go straight to voicemail. It's like... even just the thought of opening those emails makes my stomach drop, so I've just been staying away from anything related to it.
Since the blast, have you felt spaced out, numb, or like things around you aren't completely real?

No, I haven't really felt like that. I mean, I'm definitely exhausted from not sleeping, but I don't feel numb or spaced out. Everything around me feels real. I just haven't noticed anything like what you're describing.
Have you noticed feeling constantly on guard, jumpy, or easily startled since the explosion?

Yeah, I have. It's actually been pretty bad at the office. If a printer jams, or a door slams, or even if a coworker just comes up behind my desk, I practically jump out of my skin. It's like my brain instantly thinks something terrible is happening again. And then... it takes me several minutes just to settle down and get my heart rate back to normal.
